title: Dialog with a never-laid-out autowrapped Label requests a native window too large and crashes the editor via the graphics driver
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.7.stable (Arch package 5b4e0cb0f), v4.6.stable (official 89cea1439), v4.4.stable (official 4c311cbee)
- Not tested earlier, but the same zero-width-wrap trigger is reported against 3.2 in #47005 (still open), so this is long-standing rather than a regression. The claimed height varies only with default font metrics (19,254 px in 4.6/4.7; 23,258 px in 4.4).

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable (5b4e0cb0f) - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sat, 18 Jul 2026 17:30:57 +0000 on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 3 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon RX 9070 XT (radeonsi, gfx1201, ACO, DRM 3.64, 7.1.4-arch1-1) - AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor (32 threads) - 60.37 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

## AI GENERATED DISCLAIMER
I identified this bug, and generated this report and MRP with the assistance of AI (using Fable 5). However, I have independently confirmed the agent's work, reviewed all text in this issue, and confirmed the MRP and reproduction steps reliably recreates the crash.

I reliably circumvented this crash in my own project by having a static helper set Window.max_size to the usable screen rect, anytime a dialog is created that holds an autowrapped label:

```gdscript
static func cap_dialog_to_screen(dialog: Window) -> void:
	var usable := DisplayServer.screen_get_usable_rect().size
	if usable.x > 0 and usable.y > 0:
		dialog.max_size = usable
```

## Warning for Testers

> [!WARNING]
> **Note for testers:** reproducing this creates a native window ~19,000–23,000 pixels tall. On Mesa radeonsi + Wayland systems this can **crash the testing process inside the graphics driver** (SIGSEGV in `dri2_query_image`; full backtrace below) — in the originating case it repeatedly crashed the Godot editor itself — and the oversized window may briefly disrupt the compositor. Prefer testing from a terminal with no unsaved work open.

## Issue description

**What happens:** an `AcceptDialog` containing an autowrapped `Label` that has never been through a layout pass opens, on its FIRST `popup_centered()`, as a native window sized to the label's pre-layout minimum. That minimum is computed by wrapping the label's whole text at its current width — **zero** — so a one-paragraph caption claims ~19,000 px of height, and `Window` (`wrap_controls`) passes the content-derived size to the display server unclamped. Console output from the attached MRP (identical on all three versions tested, modulo the font-metric height difference):

```text
usable screen: (1920, 1080)
caption combined minimum BEFORE any layout: (1.0, 19185.0)
dialog size AFTER first popup_centered(): (716, 19254) (embedded=false)
native window size from the display server: (716, 19254)
frame 1: dialog size = (716, 19254)
...
frame 5: dialog size = (716, 19254)
ERROR: Window 2 spawned at invalid position: (602, -9087).
   at: _popup_base (scene/main/window.cpp:2282)
dialog size on SECOND popup_centered(): (716, 1080)
```

Three details worth noting: the display server really is asked for the 19,254-px-tall window (queried back via `DisplayServer.window_get_size`, not just the scene-side `size` property); the size never self-corrects while the window is shown; and the engine itself detects the absurd geometry — the "spawned at invalid position" error in `_popup_base` — but only warns about the position without clamping the size. The SECOND popup of the same dialog opens sane, because the label then has a real width from the first layout. That order-dependence made the failure look random in real applications.

Minimal construction (full script in the MRP):

```gdscript
var dlg := AcceptDialog.new()
var box := VBoxContainer.new()
box.custom_minimum_size = Vector2(700, 500)
var caption := Label.new()
caption.autowrap_mode = TextServer.AUTOWRAP_WORD_SMART
caption.text = LONG_PARAGRAPH
box.add_child(caption)
dlg.add_child(box)
add_child(dlg)
print(caption.get_combined_minimum_size())  # (1.0, 19185.0) before any layout
dlg.popup_centered()                        # native window: (716, 19254)
```

**Expected:** a dialog never asks the display server for a window taller than the screen (or at minimum, taller than the GPU can present). Nothing in the documentation prepares the user for this: [member Window.wrap_controls] is documented as "the window's size will automatically update when a child node is added or removed, ignoring min_size if the new size is bigger" — no upper bound is mentioned — and neither [method Window.popup_centered] nor [member Window.max_size] documents any clamping to screen bounds. So either the engine should clamp, or the hazard should be documented and guarded.

**How this conflicts:** the unclamped request escalates a long-known layout wart (#47005) into a process-killing crash. The oversized window can exceed the GPU's maximum surface dimension (~16384 on current AMD hardware), and on Mesa radeonsi + Wayland, presenting such a surface intermittently crashes the process inside the driver. This was discovered as a Godot **editor** crash: an editor plugin's inspection dialog (an autowrapped caption over a TextEdit — exactly the MRP's shape) reliably killed the editor on its first open after boot, and instrumentation captured a 960×21587 native window on the crash frame. Eight crash cores were collected across Mesa 26.0.6/26.1.5 before the cause was isolated; [a Mesa report has been filed in parallel for the driver's share of the blame](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/work_items/15913) (a size request should never SIGSEGV the driver), but the engine should not be requesting such windows at all.

<details>
<summary>Full crash report (Godot 4.7 editor, Mesa 26.1.5; the line above the crash block is the plugin's instrumentation printing the popup size)</summary>

```text
[gdllm-inspect] t=12118 present: popup returned, size=(960, 21587) embedded=false
[gdllm-inspect] t=12121 present: frame 1 drawn after popup

================================================================

Dumping the backtrace. Please include this when reporting the bug on: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues
```

(Frames 6–11 are misattributed symbols from the stripped distro binary; the fault frame is `dri2_query_image`, reached from Mesa's Wayland swap path — `dri2_wl_swap_buffers_with_damage` → `create_wl_buffer` per strings recovered from the cores.)

</details>

Suggested directions (either alone would defuse the crash):

- `Window::_popup_base` / `Window::_update_window_size` clamping the size requested from the display server to the usable screen area — the existing  "spawned at invalid position" check already detects the situation but only  warns about position.
- `Label::get_minimum_size` with autowrap not reporting a height wrapped at zero width before the first layout (e.g. using the custom minimum width or widest-word width as the wrap basis) — this would also resolve #47005.

Related: #47005 (same trigger, open since 3.2), #83546 (adjacent autowrap popup layout). The "spawned at invalid position" error also appears in multi-monitor position contexts (#66707, #76969, #67002) — those are position miscalculations and distinct from the unclamped size reported here.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached project and press Run (or `godot --path .`).
2. Read the console: the first popup prints a dialog size and native window size of ~716×19,254 on a 1080p screen; the second popup of the same dialog prints sane. No interaction is needed; the project quits itself.

Or in any project: create an `AcceptDialog`, add a `VBoxContainer` containing an autowrapped `Label` with a paragraph of text, call `popup_centered()` on a viewport with `gui_embed_subwindows = false`, and print `dialog.size`.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Attached: `godot-window-size-mrp.zip` — one Node script that builds the dialog, pops it twice, and prints every measurement above. Native subwindows and GL Compatibility are configured to match the editor environment where the crash occurred; the oversized request itself reproduces regardless of renderer.

[godot-window-size-mrp.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30209426/godot-window-size-mrp.zip)
